_source: 2300AD Core Book 1, chargen extract, printed p12 (pdf 6).
_replaces: The Traveller Core Rulebook Drifter career, wholesale. 2300AD drops the Barbarian assignment and adds Freelancer; Wanderer and Scavenger carry over unchanged.
_CURRENCY_RESOLVED: This table settles the Livre question. Its Cash column reads None, None, Lv1000, Lv2000, Lv3000, Lv4000, Lv8000 -- the SAME NUMBERS as the Traveller Drifter's Cr column. So 2300AD reuses Traveller's cash values 1:1 and only relabels the unit. The warning in ageing-and-mustering.json can be downgraded: reuse the Traveller Cash columns as-is and print Lv.
name: Drifter
blurb: Drifters are wanderers and Travellers, moving across colony worlds and the built-up cities of the Core. They live from job to job, relying on their wits and skills. Many are products of the extreme labour crisis of the Core, with 40%+ unemployment in most developed nations.
basic_training_exception: Use the ASSIGNMENT skill table for basic training, not Service Skills.
_structure_note: As in Traveller, the Drifter has NO Advanced Education table -- four skill tables, not five.

assignments.name: Freelancer
assignments.desc: You are a professional who works contract-to-contract, skilled in technical work but unable or unwilling to obtain steady employment.

assignments.name: Wanderer
assignments.desc: You are a consummate nomad, living hand to mouth in slums and spaceports across human space.

assignments.name: Scavenger
assignments.desc: You work as a belter (asteroid miner) or on a salvage crew.

_assignment_note: Freelancer is the new one. Wanderer and Scavenger keep the Traveller targets exactly (END 7+/INT 7+ and DEX 7+/END 7+).
_skill_table_note: Personal Development, Service Skills, Wanderer and Scavenger are byte-for-byte the Traveller Drifter's. Only the Freelancer column is new.
_rank_note: Wanderer and Scavenger rank tracks are identical to Traveller's. Freelancer is new and is the only Drifter track with three bonuses.
_cash_note: Rolls 1 and 2 pay nothing ('None'), as in Traveller. Values are Livres.

mishaps.text: Severely injured (as a result of 2 on the Injury table). Alternatively, roll twice on the Injury table and take the lower result.
Injured. Roll on the Injury table.
You run afoul of a criminal gang, corrupt bureaucrat or other foe. Gain an Enemy.
You suffer from a life-threatening illness. Reduce your END by 1.

Betrayed by a friend. One of your Contacts or Allies betrays you, ending your career; that Contact or Ally becomes a Rival or Enemy. If you have none, you are betrayed by someone you never saw coming and still gain a Rival or Enemy. In addition, roll 2D; on a 2 you must take the Prisoner career next term.
You do not know what happened to you. There is a gap in your memory.

events.text: Disaster! Roll on the Mishap table, but you are not ejected from this career.
A patron offers you a chance at a job. If you accept, gain DM+4 to your next qualification roll but you owe that patron a favour.
You pick up a few useful skills here and there. Gain one level of Jack-of-all-Trades, Survival, Streetwise or Melee.
You manage to scavenge something of use. Gain DM+1 to any one Benefit roll.
You encounter something unusual. Go to the Life Events table and have an Unusual Event.
Life Event. Roll on the Life Events table.
You are attacked by enemies. Gain an Enemy if you do not have one already, and roll either Melee 8+, Gun Combat 8+ or Stealth 8+ to avoid a roll on the Injury table.

You are offered a chance at a risky but rewarding adventure. If you accept, roll 1D: on 1-2 you are injured or arrested (roll on the Injury table or take the Prisoner career next term); on 3-4 you survive but gain nothing; on 5-6 you succeed and gain DM+4 to any one Benefit roll.
Life on the edge hones your abilities. Increase any skill you already have by one level.
You are forcibly drafted. Roll for the Draft next term.
You thrive on adversity. You are automatically promoted.

_QUESTION_ANSWERED: The tables on printed p13 are THIS career's mishaps and events, reprinted because the whole Drifter career is reprinted -- NOT a global replacement for every career's tables. Compared line by line against the Traveller Drifter and they are identical, bar one cosmetic difference: event 4 says 'Melee' where Traveller says 'Melee (any)'. Every other 2300AD career therefore keeps its Traveller mishap and event tables untouched.
